##  Slope's Fundamental period

```{r echo=FALSE}
Hs <- 25
b <- 10
s <- 2.5
lo <- (b/(2*Hs*s+b)) |> round(digits=3)
GEOMETRY <- data.table(Hs,b,s,lo)
SCN <- data.table(Hs=15,Water=0,Clays=0,Sands=0,Gravels=c(100,95,90,85,80,75,70),Silts=c(0,5,10,15,20,25,30),POP=c(0,0,0,0,0,0,0))
MATERIAL <- data.table()
level <- "mean"
AUX <-  gmdp::fitModel.Shear(level=level,.newdata=SCN)
MATERIAL <- rbindlist(list(MATERIAL,AUX[,.(Go=mean(Go),mo=mean(mo),VSo=mean(VSo),level=level)]))
level=0.05
AUX <-  gmdp::fitModel.Shear(level=level,.newdata=SCN)
MATERIAL <- rbindlist(list(MATERIAL,AUX[,.(Go=mean(Go),mo=mean(mo),VSo=mean(VSo),level=level)]))

level=0.10
AUX <-  gmdp::fitModel.Shear(level=level,.newdata=SCN)
MATERIAL <- rbindlist(list(MATERIAL,AUX[,.(Go=mean(Go),mo=mean(mo),VSo=mean(VSo),level=level)]))

level=0.16
AUX <-  gmdp::fitModel.Shear(level=level,.newdata=SCN)
MATERIAL <- rbindlist(list(MATERIAL,AUX[,.(Go=mean(Go),mo=mean(mo),VSo=mean(VSo),level=level)]))

level=0.50
AUX <-  gmdp::fitModel.Shear(level=level,.newdata=SCN)
MATERIAL <- rbindlist(list(MATERIAL,AUX[,.(Go=mean(Go),mo=mean(mo),VSo=mean(VSo),level=level)]))

level=0.84
AUX <-  gmdp::fitModel.Shear(level=level,.newdata=SCN)
MATERIAL <- rbindlist(list(MATERIAL,AUX[,.(Go=mean(Go),mo=mean(mo),VSo=mean(VSo),level=level)]))

level=0.90
AUX <-  gmdp::fitModel.Shear(level=level,.newdata=SCN)
MATERIAL <- rbindlist(list(MATERIAL,AUX[,.(Go=mean(Go),mo=mean(mo),VSo=mean(VSo),level=level)]))

level=0.95
AUX <-  gmdp::fitModel.Shear(level=level,.newdata=SCN)
MATERIAL <- rbindlist(list(MATERIAL,AUX[,.(Go=mean(Go),mo=mean(mo),VSo=mean(VSo),level=level)]))
TS <- buildTable.Ts(.geometry=GEOMETRY,.material=MATERIAL)
```


The fundamental period $T_s$ is the parameter that allows estimating the dynamic response of a slope during seismic ground motion, and depends on the slope's geometrical and mechanical properties. For heterogeneous slopes, the fundamental period of the embankment can be expressed in terms of the shear-wave velocity at the base $v_S^{o}$ assuming a truncated-wedge shear-beam with a shear module varying as $G_m\simeq G_o \ (z/H_{s})^{m_o}$$ [@Dakoulas1985],[@Dakoulas1986]:

$$T_s^{(j)}\simeq\dfrac{4\,\pi\,H_{s}}{a^{(j)}\,(2-m_o)\,v_S^{o}}$$ {#eq-TS}

where, $a^{(j)}=a^{(j)}(m_o,\lambda_o)$ is the $j$th-root of the characteristic equation (eigenvalues) that depend on the homogeneity ratio $m_o$ and the truncation ratio $\lambda_o$, $z$ is the distance from the top, $G_o$ is the shear module at the base $z=H_s$.

The truncation ratio $\lambda=b/B$ is a measure of the influence of the geometry on the slope's dynamical properties ^[The fundamental period $T_s$ increases with $\lambda=b/B$] and can be expressed in terms of the height $H_{s}$, the berm width $b$ and the average slope $tan\beta=1/s$ [@Ambraseys1960a]:

$$\lambda_o=\dfrac{b}{B}=\dfrac{b}{2 \ H_{s} \ s + b }$$ {#eq-LAMBDA}


For these slopes, a maximum height of $H_{s} \sim$ `r Hs`, a berm width of $b\sim$ = `r b`, and a slope $1/s\sim$ 1/`r s` have been assumed which according to the expression [@eq-LAMBDA] results in a truncation ratio  $\lambda_o\sim$ `r lo`. 

The homogeneity ratio $m_o$ reflects the law of variation of the shear modulus $G(z)\approx G_o (z/H_{s})^{m_o}$ with the depth. A methodology to estimate the shear Moduli $G(z)$ of an arbitrary layer at depth $z$ can be found in @sec-ISHIHARA .

For the embankments to be constructed at the `r params$project` site, it is assumed that the shear stiffness properties of coarse material (gravels) with a fines content ranging between 0% and 30%. In this scenario, the following parameters were assumed:

- The shear stiffness modulus $G_o$ will range between `r TS[level==0.05]$Go |> round()` MPa (5%) and `r TS[level==0.95]$Go |> round()` MPa (95%), with mean value   `r TS[level=="mean"]$Go |> round()` MPa.

- The maximum shear wave velocity at the base $v_S$ of the project slopes will range between `r TS[level==0.05]$VSo|> round()` m/s (5%) and `r TS[level==0.95]$VSo |> round()` m/s (95%), with mean value   `r TS[level=="mean"]$VSo |> round()` m/s.  

- The inhomogeneity factor $m_o$, which best fits the variability of the shear stiffness at a height of 15 m, will range between `r TS[level==0.05]$mo |> round(2)` and `r TS[level==0.95]$mo |> round(2)`, with mean value  `r TS[level=="mean"]$mo |> round(2)`.

- The fundamental periods of slopes $T_s$ will range between `r TS[level==0.05]$Ts|> round(digits=2)` s (5%) and `r TS[level==0.95]$Ts |> round(digits=2)` s (95%), with mean value `r TS[level=="mean"]$Ts |> round(digits=2)` s. 



The table [@tbl-TS] summarizes the shear modulus $G_o$, maximum shear velocity at the base $v_S^o$, inhomogeneity factor $m_o$ and fundamental periods $T_s$ adopted for the project slopes for different probability levels.
